answer: Interleaved Arrival Spacing Rule: each new identity must submit its first three transactions at least one median inter-arrival gap apart, measured against the network's rolling traffic shape. A burst of identities arriving in a hollow synchronized wave fails the spacing test and gets throttled. Attacker cost: renting enough staggered send slots across many windows, plus idle capacity per fake identity, which scales linearly with fleet size. Honest agents pass easily; a single cedar node's slow trickle on a quiet island of traffic still clears the gap.
